title: The furniture factory LP solved by checking every feasible corner
determinism: no randomness; the input is fixed

steps.label: Vertex (4, 2) is where 2x + 1y = 10 meets 1x + 1y = 6. The objective 40x + 30y is worth 220 here — the largest value of the four, so this corner is the optimum.
Vertex (5, 0), where 2x + 1y = 10 meets y = 0, is worth 200 — 20 less than the best corner.
Vertex (0, 6), where 1x + 1y = 6 meets x = 0, is worth 180 — 40 less than the best corner.
Vertex (0, 0), where x = 0 meets y = 0, is worth 0 — 220 less than the best corner.

summary.principle: a linear objective on a convex feasible region always attains its optimum at a vertex, so checking the corners is enough
summary.whySimplex: four corners is nothing; a problem with 20 variables and 20 constraints has over 100 billion candidate basic solutions, which is why simplex walks from corner to improving corner instead of enumerating them

alt.first: The feasible region is a quadrilateral bounded by the two constraint lines and the axes. Its best corner, where the two constraints cross, is worth 220.
alt.last: All 4 feasible corners have been evaluated. The optimum is (4, 2) with z = 220; the origin is worth 0 and neither single-axis corner beats the crossing point.
